question: Show me detailed visual analytics and statistics of inspection scores across all establishments.
output_text:
## Scope and coverage
This analysis covers **7,798 inspections with a recorded score**, spanning **1,291 SLCHD listings**. The broader Google-place dataset contains **8,592 establishments**, but only **139 (1.6%)** have a matched SLCHD inspection-history link; therefore, these score statistics describe the available inspection records—not every restaurant in the Google dataset. A missing match is not evidence of a clean inspection record.

## Overall score distribution
- **Mean:** **10.29** points; **median:** **7** points.
- **Middle 50%:** scores from **3** (25th percentile) to **14** (75th percentile).
- **Standard deviation:** **12.07**, indicating a right-skewed distribution with a smaller number of much higher scores.
- Observed range: **0 to 297**.

The distribution chart shows that the most common band is **4–9 points**: **2,371 inspections (30.4%)**. Another **1,635 (21.0%)** scored **1–3**, and **710 (9.1%)** scored **0**. Together, **4,716 inspections (60.5%)** scored from 0 through 9. At the higher end, **1,994 (25.6%)** scored **10–19**, while **1,088 (14.0%)** scored **20 or more**.

## Change over time
Annual average scores rose into the low teens in the mid-2010s and early 2020s, then declined in the most recent years in the dataset:
- **2015:** mean **13.00**, median **11** (77 scored inspections).
- **2022:** mean **12.08**, median **9** (869 inspections).
- **2023:** mean **12.01**, median **8** (879 inspections).
- **2024:** mean **11.49**, median **8** (1,227 inspections).
- **2025:** mean **8.90**, median **6** (1,343 inspections).
- **2026:** mean **6.33**, median **5** (865 inspections).

Interpret the early years cautiously because their inspection counts are small—for example, only **3** scored inspections in 2009 and **5** in 2010. Also, the 2026 figure reflects the records currently present rather than necessarily a complete calendar year.

## Scores by inspection type
- **Routine:** **7,380** scored inspections; mean **10.45**, median **8**.
- **Critical Item:** **202**; mean **9.02**, median **3**.
- **Followup:** **211**; mean **6.19**, median **3**.
- **Complaint Investigation:** **5**; mean **1.80**, median **0**.

Routine inspections dominate the dataset (**94.6%** of scored inspections), so they largely determine the countywide distribution. Comparisons across inspection types should be cautious: follow-up and critical-item visits are purpose-specific rather than directly comparable to routine inspections, and complaint investigations have only five scored records.

## Key takeaway
Inspection scores are concentrated at the lower end of the observed scale: the median is **7**, and **60.5%** of scored inspections fall between **0 and 9**. The mean of **10.29** exceeds the median because relatively infrequent high-score inspections pull the average upward; the maximum recorded score is **297**.

  category varchar
}

Table establishments {
  gmap_id varchar [pk]
  name varchar
  address varchar
  description varchar
  geom geometry [note: 'ST_Point(longitude, latitude), spatial extension']
  avg_rating double
  num_of_reviews integer
  price varchar
  slchd_establishment_key varchar [ref: > establishment_keys.slchd_establishment_key, note: 'nullable; set when ER matched']

  Note: 'One row per Google Local place — all restaurants, not just SLCHD-matched.'
}

Table establishment_attributes {
  gmap_id varchar [ref: > establishments.gmap_id, not null]
  attribute varchar [not null]

  indexes { (gmap_id, attribute) [pk] }

  Note: 'Flattened meta.MISC leaf values. Outer category label (e.g. "Service options") dropped.'
}

Table establishment_categories {
  gmap_id varchar [ref: > establishments.gmap_id, not null]
  category_id integer [ref: > category.category_id, not null]

  indexes { (gmap_id, category_id) [pk] }
}

Table gmap_hours {
  gmap_id varchar [ref: > establishments.gmap_id, not null]
  day integer [not null, note: '0=Sun … 6=Sat']
  open_min bigint
  open_max bigint

  indexes { (gmap_id, day) [pk] }

  Note: 'Covers every meta place with parsable hours, not just the SLCHD-matched subset.'
}

Table review {
  user_id varchar
  name varchar
  time bigint
  rating double
  text varchar
  resp varchar
  gmap_id varchar [ref: > establishments.gmap_id]
}

Table inspection_types {
  inspection_type_id integer [pk, note: 'parsed leading number, e.g. "01 - Routine" -> 1']
  description varchar [note: 'e.g. "Routine"']
}

Table inspections {
  inspection_id bigint [pk, increment]
  slchd_establishment_key varchar [ref: > establishment_keys.slchd_establishment_key, not null]
  inspection_date date [not null]
  inspection_type_id integer [ref: > inspection_types.inspection_type_id, note: 'nullable — 27 rows have no type']
  inspection_score integer

  Note: 'One row per inspection visit. count_critical/noncritical_violations dropped (derivable from violations).'
}

Table violation_codes {
  violation_code_id integer [pk, increment]
  code_text varchar [not null, note: 'base code, asterisks stripped, e.g. "4.5.18"']
  asterisk_count integer [not null, note: '0/1/2 trailing * in source, meaning unconfirmed']
  critical boolean [not null]
}

Table violations {
  violation_id bigint [pk, increment]
  inspection_id bigint [ref: > inspections.inspection_id, not null]
  violation_code_id integer [ref: > violation_codes.violation_code_id, not null]
  violation_description varchar [note: 'per-occurrence free text']
  violation_occurrences integer
  violation_cos boolean [note: 'corrected on site']
  violation_phr varchar [note: 'public health rationale']

  Note: 'One row per violation actually cited. Zero-violation inspections get zero rows (no placeholder row).'
}

Action: run_sql({'query': 'WITH scored AS (SELECT inspection_score FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL) SELECT COUNT(*) AS inspections_with_score, COUNT(DISTINCT slchd_establishment_key) AS establishments_with_scored_inspection, MIN(inspection_score) AS min_score, MAX(inspection_score) AS max_score, ROUND(AVG(inspection_score),2) AS mean_score, MEDIAN(inspection_score) AS median_score, STDDEV_SAMP(inspection_score) AS sd_score, QUANTILE_CONT(inspection_score, 0.25) AS p25_score, QUANTILE_CONT(inspection_score, 0.75) AS p75_score FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL;'})

Action: run_sql({'query': "SELECT CASE WHEN inspection_score = 0 THEN '0' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN '1–3' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 4 AND 9 THEN '4–9' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 10 AND 19 THEN '10–19' WHEN inspection_score >= 20 THEN '20+' END AS score_band, COUNT(*) AS inspection_count, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS percent_of_scored_inspections FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CASE score_band WHEN '0' THEN 1 WHEN '1–3' THEN 2 WHEN '4–9' THEN 3 WHEN '10–19' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END;"})

Action: run_sql({'query': 'SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM inspection_date)::INTEGER AS inspection_year, COUNT(*) AS scored_inspections, ROUND(AVG(inspection_score),2) AS mean_score, MEDIAN(inspection_score) AS median_score, MIN(inspection_score) AS min_score, MAX(inspection_score) AS max_score FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;'})

Action: run_sql({'query': 'SELECT it.description AS inspection_type, COUNT(*) AS scored_inspections, ROUND(AVG(i.inspection_score),2) AS mean_score, MEDIAN(i.inspection_score) AS median_score, MIN(i.inspection_score) AS min_score, MAX(i.inspection_score) AS max_score FROM inspections i LEFT JOIN inspection_types it ON i.inspection_type_id = it.inspection_type_id WHERE i.inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY scored_inspections DESC;'})

Action: run_sql({'query': 'SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_google_establishments, COUNT(slchd_establishment_key) AS matched_establishments, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(slchd_establishment_key) / COUNT(*), 1) AS matched_pct FROM establishments;'})

SELECT CASE WHEN inspection_score = 0 THEN '0' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN '1–3' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 4 AND 9 THEN '4–9' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 10 AND 19 THEN '10–19' WHEN inspection_score >= 20 THEN '20+' END AS score_band, COUNT(*) AS inspection_count, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 1) AS percent_of_scored_inspections FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CASE score_band WHEN '0' THEN 1 WHEN '1–3' THEN 2 WHEN '4–9' THEN 3 WHEN '10–19' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END;

SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM inspection_date)::INTEGER AS inspection_year, COUNT(*) AS scored_inspections, ROUND(AVG(inspection_score),2) AS mean_score, MEDIAN(inspection_score) AS median_score, MIN(inspection_score) AS min_score, MAX(inspection_score) AS max_score FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

SELECT it.description AS inspection_type, COUNT(*) AS scored_inspections, ROUND(AVG(i.inspection_score),2) AS mean_score, MEDIAN(i.inspection_score) AS median_score, MIN(i.inspection_score) AS min_score, MAX(i.inspection_score) AS max_score FROM inspections i LEFT JOIN inspection_types it ON i.inspection_type_id = it.inspection_type_id WHERE i.inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY scored_inspections DESC;

args.query: SELECT CASE WHEN inspection_score = 0 THEN '0' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 1 AND 3 THEN '1–3' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 4 AND 9 THEN '4–9' WHEN inspection_score BETWEEN 10 AND 19 THEN '10–19' WHEN inspection_score >= 20 THEN '20+' END AS score_band, COUNT(*) AS inspection_count FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY CASE score_band WHEN '0' THEN 1 WHEN '1–3' THEN 2 WHEN '4–9' THEN 3 WHEN '10–19' THEN 4 ELSE 5 END;
args.title: Distribution of Salt Lake County Inspection Scores (7,798 scored inspections)

args.query: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM inspection_date)::INTEGER AS inspection_year, ROUND(AVG(inspection_score),2) AS mean_score, MEDIAN(inspection_score) AS median_score FROM inspections WHERE inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
args.title: Annual Mean and Median Inspection Scores

args.query: SELECT it.description AS inspection_type, COUNT(*) AS scored_inspections, ROUND(AVG(i.inspection_score),2) AS mean_score FROM inspections i LEFT JOIN inspection_types it ON i.inspection_type_id = it.inspection_type_id WHERE i.inspection_score IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY mean_score DESC;

{"establishment_name":"Salt Lake County inspection-score dataset","hypothesis":"none","confidence":"high","narrative_answer":"## Scope and coverage
This analysis covers **7,798 inspections with a recorded score**, spanning **1,291 SLCHD listings**. The broader Google-place dataset contains **8,592 establishments**, but only **139 (1.6%)** have a matched SLCHD inspection-history link; therefore, these score statistics describe the available inspection records—not every restaurant in the Google dataset. A missing match is not evidence of a clean inspection record.

## Overall score distribution
- **Mean:** **10.29** points; **median:** **7** points.
- **Middle 50%:** scores from **3** (25th percentile) to **14** (75th percentile).
- **Standard deviation:** **12.07**, indicating a right-skewed distribution with a smaller number of much higher scores.
- Observed range: **0 to 297**.

The distribution chart shows that the most common band is **4–9 points**: **2,371 inspections (30.4%)**. Another **1,635 (21.0%)** scored **1–3**, and **710 (9.1%)** scored **0**. Together, **4,716 inspections (60.5%)** scored from 0 through 9. At the higher end, **1,994 (25.6%)** scored **10–19**, while **1,088 (14.0%)** scored **20 or more**.

## Change over time
Annual average scores rose into the low teens in the mid-2010s and early 2020s, then declined in the most recent years in the dataset:
- **2015:** mean **13.00**, median **11** (77 scored inspections).
- **2022:** mean **12.08**, median **9** (869 inspections).
- **2023:** mean **12.01**, median **8** (879 inspections).
- **2024:** mean **11.49**, median **8** (1,227 inspections).
- **2025:** mean **8.90**, median **6** (1,343 inspections).
- **2026:** mean **6.33**, median **5** (865 inspections).

Interpret the early years cautiously because their inspection counts are small—for example, only **3** scored inspections in 2009 and **5** in 2010. Also, the 2026 figure reflects the records currently present rather than necessarily a complete calendar year.

## Scores by inspection type
- **Routine:** **7,380** scored inspections; mean **10.45**, median **8**.
- **Critical Item:** **202**; mean **9.02**, median **3**.
- **Followup:** **211**; mean **6.19**, median **3**.
- **Complaint Investigation:** **5**; mean **1.80**, median **0**.

Routine inspections dominate the dataset (**94.6%** of scored inspections), so they largely determine the countywide distribution. Comparisons across inspection types should be cautious: follow-up and critical-item visits are purpose-specific rather than directly comparable to routine inspections, and complaint investigations have only five scored records.

## Key takeaway
Inspection scores are concentrated at the lower end of the observed scale: the median is **7**, and **60.5%** of scored inspections fall between **0 and 9**.
